## Overview

In Assignment 14 you pre-trained a **base model**: it continues text but does not follow requests. In this assignment you will fine-tune it to follow a simple instruction:

```
Topic: dog
Story: Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. ...
```

| Stage | Assignment |
|---|---|
| 1. Pre-training → base model | 14 |
| 2. **Instruction tuning** → follows an instruction | **15 (this one)** |
| 3. Preference tuning → prefers better responses | 16 |

You will build the instruction data, write the key step of instruction tuning (computing the loss only on the response), fine-tune the model, and measure how often it writes about the requested topic before and after.

## What to Submit

Submit the completed notebook `assignment15_student.ipynb` on Canvas, with all cells run. **Keep the file `instruct_model.pt`** that the notebook saves: Assignment 16 starts from it.

## Files You Need

Put these files in the same folder as the notebook:

| File | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| `tiny_gpt.py` | Provided with this assignment: the model from Assignment 14, with helper functions |
| `base_model.pt` | Yours from Assignment 14. If your model did not train well, use the one provided with this assignment. |
| `tinystories.txt` | Saved by your Assignment 14 notebook |

The notebook also downloads 40 MB of new TinyStories text. Fine-tuning takes about **4–6 minutes** on a laptop CPU.

## The Questions

| Question | Topic |
|---|---|
| 1 | Build balanced instruction → response examples for 10 topics |
| 2 | How often does the base model follow the instruction? |
| 3 | Mask the prompt so that the loss counts only the response |
| 4 | Fine-tune the base model |
| 5 | Measure the on-topic rate before and after, by topic |
| 6 | Catastrophic forgetting: is the model still good at plain stories? |
| 7 | Topics the model has never seen |
| 8 | Reflection: why masking works; real instruction tuning vs. ours |

## AI Policy

You may use AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot). Include a short statement describing how you used them and anything they got wrong that you had to fix.
